hero.title: File:Calumetvictims-1913.jpg
hero.description:
Original caption: Rough boxes in which Calumet victims were buriedBelieve this is related to: Striking miners and their families were gathered on Christmas Eve for a party in Italian Hall, when the cry of "fire" precipitated a stampede that crushed or suffocated seventy-three victims, the majority of them children. The identity of the person(s) who started the stampede has never been determined. Folk singer Woody Guthrie's song, "1913 Massacre", is based on this event.

Word "suomalainen" written in the window means "the Finn" as a citizen from Finland, which also is a name of newspaper.
categories: Black and white photographs of the United States in the 1910s

gallery.title: File:Italian Hall Arch.JPG
gallery.description: This doorway arch is what remains of Italian Hall in Calumet, Michigan. The site is currently a park. There is an informational marker that lists some history including the Italian Hall disaster in which 73 people died.
categories: Files with coordinates missing SDC location of creation
Michigan Historical Markers in Houghton County, Michigan

gallery.title: File:Italian Hall disaster funeral procession - 1913.jpg
gallery.description: A funeral procession for victims of the Italian Hall disaster. The procession took place on Sunday (probably December 28, 1913) and was two miles long and lined by thousands.
categories: Funeral processions in the United States

gallery.title: File:Italian Hall caskets.png
gallery.description: Caskets shipped to Calumet, Michigan, in response to the Italian Hall disaster. Same scene, but different quality, as File:Calumetvictims-1913.jpg
